sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU primary, WebGL2 fallback), Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, BroadcastChannel, WebRTC, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded jungle dioramas, ink outlines, warm paper, coral and forest palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and original AnimationClips for idle, run, jump, climb and vine swing; procedural environmental animation
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written marimba, bass and percussion music at 10% by default; synthesized effects, ambience and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player ghost expedition races through AI Hub, local BroadcastChannel rooms, or direct WebRTC invitation/answer; Internet NAT traversal unknown
sourceInformation.testing: Native WebGPU initialization and Rapier state checks; Chromium WebGL2 visual review; complete unassisted physical playthrough; emulated gamepad and touch; offline audio levels; two-page local/WebRTC transfers; official Hub harness with latency, jitter, packet loss and host departure. No physical controller or remote Internet peer available.
sourceInformation.research: Original Atari 2600 manual: mechanics, 255-scene circular maze, 32 treasures, ladders and hazards; period visual descriptions and sound references; Three.js r180, Rapier and AI Hub documentation

testingFeedback: 12 issues found and fixed across integration tests, visual checks and review; two additional test-setup errors were corrected.
3 blocked game entry or navigation: Hub metadata, countdown start, and returning from result submenus. All are fixed.
The complete physical expedition: all 12 treasures, 3 vine crossings, 4 ladder traversals, 25 jumps, zero hits and victory, with no teleports, invincibility or collection cheats.
The initial case-sensitive visible credits-text check: CSS capitalization produced a false failure. It now checks the underlying text.
engineFeedback: Native AnimationMixer clips and toon node materials suited the procedural ink art and original explorer animations.
WebGPU initialized, but SwiftShader screenshot capture could lose the software device; native state checks and the renderer's WebGL2 backend supplied reliable verification and visual review.
The platforming controller, magnetic vine catches and releases, ladder traversal, expedition progression and controller-first menus.
Keeping pendulum art, Rapier traversal and all input methods in agreement while preserving readable side-on depth.
none; application code uses the engines without modifying their source.
A complete WebGPU game starter with controller navigation, toon outlines and deterministic physics test hooks.
promptFeedback: The source research, complete-demo scope and controller-first requirements gave the game a clear creative direction.
Multiplayer mode and topology were unspecified; a two-player ghost treasure race was chosen for both AI Hub and standalone play.
Combining a complete physical expedition, procedural art/audio, four input methods and online races into one shareable HTML file.
Specify the intended multiplayer mode and whether direct peer invitations are desired alongside AI Hub sessions.

aiHub.name: Pit Perfect
aiHub.description: Keep your hat on in an ink-lined jungle adventure. Leap logs, catch vines, brave crocodile crossings and hunt twelve treasures above and below ground, alone or in a friendly ghost race.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / A D / arrows; jump and vine release: Cross / Space; ladders and vines: Square / E / up-down; pause: Options / Esc; touch: left drag and right tap.
